reading.body:
J-Curve Technologies cannot be counted as an Arizona data center, because no operator, registration, or coverage confirms it exists at the Tempe address.

The entry rests on a single OpenStreetMap node at coordinates that reverse geocode to 2005 West 14th Street, Tempe, with no business name attached. No website, business registration, or press coverage was found, and the research status is exhausted. The name itself is a finance term for a growth pattern, not an established technology brand. This is an unconfirmed record, not a facility.

The pattern matters because Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities and only 4 publish power specifications, totaling 512 MW. A row like this one sits outside that count entirely. It carries no megawatts, no operator, and no evidence of server rooms or colocation space, so it cannot be ranked against the facilities that do publish specifications.

For AI scaling, the binding constraint is grid load, and grid load is measured from facilities that can be identified and metered. This one cannot. The data does not show that a data center is absent from the site, only that no public evidence establishes one. It also does not connect this address to any other facility in the batch, which sits more than 20 miles from the nearest rows.
